newsitem.title: UK: UK pension funds say tax credit impact not major.
newsitem.headline: UK pension funds say tax credit impact not major.

text.p: The National Association of Pension Funds said Britain's decision to abolish tax credits for share buybacks and "special" dividends would affect returns for its members but the effect would not be significant.

"It will reduce the investment returns for pension funds and PEP (personal equity plan) holders but not significantly...We believe it's a responsible move," said a spokeswoman for the NAPF told Reuters.
She said the NAPF was not surprised by the action, just by its timing, ahead of the November budget. "But we acknowledge it restores the level playing field for all investors," she added.
She said the NAPF's budget submission to the government focused on tax credits on ordinary dividends.
"We've asked for the restoration of the value of tax credits on ordinary dividends to 24 percent (from a current 20 percent)," she said.

Referring to the impact of the abolition of tax credits for share buybacks and special dividends related to takeovers or share buybacks, she said it would be limited as most pension funds held diversified equity portfolios which would only contain a handful of companies who had announced such buybacks or special dividends.
She added as the Chancellor stood to make substantial savings from the new ruling, which is effective October 8, she was hopeful that he might find some way of returning this cash.
The government said in a statement that it expected to make savings of 400 million pounds a year from 1998-99 as a result of the changes in tax legislation.
